memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me along with anything containing yeast, and do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover Festival remain until morning. Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.'" - Exod 34:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three brief instructions, easy to skim past. But each carries something worth seeing.

Yeast spreads quietly through dough, and Scripture uses it as a picture of how sin works. Paul says a little yeast leavens the whole batch and urges the church to get rid of the old yeast (1 Cor 5:6-8). Small compromises do not stay small.

Nothing left till morning: the Passover was to be dealt with completely, at the appointed time. There is an urgency in obedience. What God gives us to do today should not be shelved.

"The best of the firstfruits" — not the leftovers. God asks for the first and the finest. Malachi later rebukes Israel for offering blind and lame animals, asking whether they would dare present such gifts to their governor (Mal 1:8). The question exposes what our giving reveals about our view of God.

The goat and its mother's milk is likely a rejection of a Canaanite fertility practice, and possibly a guard against cruelty — using the source of life to prepare death. God cares about how His people do things, not just what they do.

What are you giving God — your first and best, or what remains after everything else?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "little yeast" are you tolerating right now?
2. Does God receive your first and best, or your leftovers?
3. Is there an obedience you have been postponing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, take the first and best of my time, my resources and my energy. Remove the small compromises I have allowed. Amen.
